```{r header, child="header.Rmd"}
```

```{r params}
if (!exists("base_dir")) {base_dir = "~/projects/templeton/results"}
if (!exists("datasets")) {datasets = c("AlphaSperm", "EGAD00001005795")}
if (!exists("pattern")) {pattern = "^dmrcombp.*\\.regions-t\\.bed$"}
if (!exists("EXPORT_XLSX")) {EXPORT_XLSX = FALSE}
```

- `base_dir` = "`r base_dir`" is the folder containing one sub-folder of results per dataset.
- `datasets` = `r paste(datasets, collapse = ", ")`.
- `EXPORT_XLSX` = `r EXPORT_XLSX` controls whether the per-model result tables are merged in a single Excel workbook (`FALSE` by default).


# Load `combp` DMRs

One `.regions-t.bed` file per model and per dataset. The model name is extracted from the file name (the part after `~`) and prefixed by the dataset name.

```{r load_dmrs, results="verbatim"}
files = unlist(lapply(datasets, function(ds) {
  list.files(file.path(base_dir, ds), pattern = pattern, full.names = TRUE)
}))

models = basename(files)
models = sub("^.*~", "", models)
models = sub("\\.regions-t\\.bed$", "", models)
models = paste0(basename(dirname(files)), "_", models)

dmrs = lapply(files, function(f) {
  print(f)
  read.table(f, header = FALSE, sep = "\t")
})
names(dmrs) = models

# Dataset of each model
dataset_of = setNames(basename(dirname(files)), models)



# Sort models by dataset, then by formula, then by numeric threshold
ds = dataset_of[models]

# Model name without the dataset prefix
model_only = unname(mapply(function(m, d) sub(paste0("^", d, "_"), "", m), models, ds))

# Threshold = trailing "_<number>", plain (0.05) or scientific (1e-5, 1e-10)
thr_regex = "_([0-9.]+([eE][-+]?[0-9]+)?)$"
has_thr = grepl(thr_regex, model_only)
threshold = rep(NA_real_, length(model_only))
threshold[has_thr] = as.numeric(sub(paste0("^.*", thr_regex), "\\1", model_only[has_thr]))

# Formula = model name without the threshold
formula_only = sub(thr_regex, "", model_only)

# Ascending threshold (1e-20 first); use -threshold for the strictest last
ord = order(factor(ds, levels = datasets), formula_only, threshold, na.last = TRUE)
models = models[ord]
dmrs = dmrs[models]

# Check the result
print(data.frame(dataset = ds[ord], formula = formula_only[ord], threshold = threshold[ord], row.names = NULL))
```


# Number of DMRs per model

```{r recap, results="verbatim"}
recap = data.frame(
  model   = models,
  dataset = dataset_of[models],
  nb_DMR  = sapply(dmrs, nrow),
  row.names = NULL
)
print(recap, row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(recap, "dmr_recap.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r recap_barplot, fig.width=12, fig.height=8}
library(ggplot2)

# Barplot: keep the same order as models (first model on top)
p = ggplot(recap, aes(x = factor(model, levels = rev(models)), y = nb_DMR, fill = dataset)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_text(aes(label = nb_DMR), hjust = -0.2, size = 3) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Number of DMRs", fill = "Dataset") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "top"
  )
print(p)
ggsave("dmr_counts_barplot.pdf", p, width = 12, height = 8)
```


# Overlap between models

## Pairwise comparison

A region of A is *common* if it overlaps at least one region of B (same chromosome, overlapping intervals).

```{r overlap_function}
# Count regions in A overlapping at least one region in B
count_overlap = function(a, b) {
  sum(sapply(seq_len(nrow(a)), function(i) {
    any(b[[1]] == a[i, 1] &
        b[[2]] < a[i, 3] &
        b[[3]] > a[i, 2])
  }))
}
```

```{r pairwise, results="verbatim"}
pairs = combn(models, 2, simplify = FALSE)

comparisons = do.call(rbind, lapply(pairs, function(p) {
  a = dmrs[[p[1]]]
  b = dmrs[[p[2]]]

  n_common_a = count_overlap(a, b)
  n_common_b = count_overlap(b, a)

  data.frame(
    model_A  = p[1],
    model_B  = p[2],
    n_A      = nrow(a),
    n_B      = nrow(b),
    common_A = n_common_a,
    common_B = n_common_b,
    unique_A = nrow(a) - n_common_a,
    unique_B = nrow(b) - n_common_b
  )
}))

print(comparisons, row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(comparisons, "dmr_pairwise.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

## Heatmap of the percentage of overlapping DMRs

Each cell gives the percentage of DMRs of the model in row (A) overlapping at least one DMR of the model in column (B). The matrix is therefore not symmetric.

```{r overlap_matrix}
n = length(models)
overlap_mat = matrix(
  NA_real_,
  nrow = n,
  ncol = n,
  dimnames = list(models, models)
)

for (i in seq_along(models)) {
  for (j in seq_along(models)) {
    a = dmrs[[i]]
    b = dmrs[[j]]
    if (nrow(a) > 0) {
      overlap_mat[i, j] = 100 * count_overlap(a, b) / nrow(a)
    }
  }
}

# Long format for ggplot
heatmap_df = as.data.frame(as.table(overlap_mat))
colnames(heatmap_df) = c("model_A", "model_B", "overlap")
# Heatmap: keep the dataset order in the facets (alphabetical by default)
heatmap_df$type_A = factor(dataset_of[as.character(heatmap_df$model_A)], levels = datasets)
heatmap_df$type_B = factor(dataset_of[as.character(heatmap_df$model_B)], levels = datasets)
```

```{r overlap_heatmap, fig.width=16, fig.height=12}
# White = exactly 0, then lightgrey -> steelblue for non-zero values
p = ggplot(heatmap_df, aes(x = model_B, y = model_A, fill = overlap)) +
  geom_tile(color = "grey90", linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(
    # Sharp step right above 0: white at 0, lightgrey just after, steelblue at 100
    colours = c("white", "white", "lightgrey", "steelblue"),
    values  = scales::rescale(c(0, 0.01, 0.02, 100), from = c(0, 100)),
    limits  = c(0, 100),
    name    = "Overlapping\nDMRs (%)",
    na.value = "grey90"
  ) +
  facet_grid(type_A ~ type_B, scales = "free", space = "free") +
  coord_equal() +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5, size = 7),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7),
    axis.title  = element_blank(),
    panel.grid  = element_blank(),
    strip.text  = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "right"
  )
print(p)
ggsave("dmr_overlap_heatmap.pdf", plot = p, width = 16, height = 12)
```


# Merge result tables in a single Excel workbook

Optional step (`EXPORT_XLSX = TRUE`): one sheet per model, plus an `INDEX` sheet linking sheet names to the original files.

```{r export_xlsx, eval=EXPORT_XLSX, results="verbatim"}
library(readxl)
library(openxlsx)

files_xlsx = list(
  mcc  = list.files(file.path(base_dir, "mcc_sa"),
                    pattern = "^global_results_peaks5_.*\\.xlsx$", full.names = TRUE),
  chip = list.files(file.path(base_dir, "chip_sa"),
                    pattern = "^dmrcombp_peaks5_deseq2_.*\\.xlsx$", full.names = TRUE)
)

wb = createWorkbook()
index = data.frame(sheet = character(), dataset = character(), filename = character())

i = 0
for (prefix in names(files_xlsx)) {
  for (f in files_xlsx[[prefix]]) {
    i = i + 1

    # Extract the model formula from the filename
    model = basename(f)
    model = sub("\\.xlsx$", "", model)
    model = sub("^global_results_peaks5_~", "", model)
    model = sub("^dmrcombp_peaks5_deseq2_~", "", model)
    model = sub("_0\\.05$", "", model)

    # Excel sheet names are limited to 31 characters
    sheet = paste0(prefix, "_", sprintf("%02d", i), "_", substr(model, 1, 20))
    message("Importing: ", basename(f), " -> ", sheet)

    df = read_excel(f)
    addWorksheet(wb, sheet)
    writeData(wb, sheet, df, withFilter = TRUE)
    freezePane(wb, sheet, firstRow = TRUE)

    index = rbind(index, data.frame(
      sheet    = sheet,
      dataset  = basename(dirname(f)),
      filename = basename(f)
    ))
  }
}

addWorksheet(wb, "INDEX")
writeData(wb, "INDEX", index, withFilter = TRUE)
setColWidths(wb, "INDEX", cols = 1:3, widths = "auto")

output = file.path(base_dir, "all_DMR_results.xlsx")
saveWorkbook(wb, output, overwrite = TRUE)
message("Created: ", output, " (", i, " files imported)")
```
